title: Hope Fund Week 2026: Colleagues caring for each other when they need it most
summary: The HCA Healthcare Hope Fund provides financial assistance to colleagues and their families during unexpected times of need.
body_markdown:
**Key takeaways:**


- The HCA Healthcare Hope Fund provides financial assistance to colleagues and their families following an unexpected event, including illness, injury and natural disasters.
- Since 2005, The HCA Healthcare Hope Fund has provided more than $132 million in assistance to more than 52,000 HCA Healthcare colleagues and their families.
- During Hope Fund Week, learn how five colleagues found support through the Hope Fund during unexpected circumstances and how colleagues across HCA Healthcare help make this support possible for others.


At HCA Healthcare, caring for others extends beyond the patients and communities we are privileged to serve. It also means being there for one another during life’s unexpected moments.


One way this commitment comes to life is through the[HCA Healthcare Hope Fund](https://www.hcahopefund.com/) , which provides financial assistance to HCA Healthcare colleagues and their families, helping them navigate circumstances including illness, injury, natural disasters and other unexpected events. Since 2005, the Hope Fund has provided over $132 million in assistance to more than 52,000 HCA Healthcare colleagues and their families.


Made possible by the generosity of donors, the Hope Fund is a resource HCA Healthcare colleagues can turn to for support when unexpected circumstances arise.


> *“Through the HCA Healthcare Hope Fund, we have the opportunity to care for our colleagues when they need it most. In 2025, we provided over $9.5 million in assistance to colleagues during times of need, reflecting the kindness and generosity that are at the heart of how we support one another. Thank you for caring for each other like family and helping our colleagues feel supported through life’s most difficult moments.”*
>
>
> *CHAD WASSERMAN, SENIOR VICE PRESIDENT AND CHIEF INFORMATION OFFICER* , HCA HEALTHCARE


## How the HCA Healthcare Hope Fund began


The HCA Healthcare Hope Fund traces its roots to the 2004 hurricane season, when Hurricanes Charley, Frances, Ivan and Jeanne caused widespread devastation across Florida and other parts of the Southeastern United States. Florida was particularly hard hit, with all four hurricanes impacting the state in a matter of weeks. HCA Healthcare colleagues responded by contributing funds to help fellow colleagues and their families who had been affected by the storms.


That informal effort to help colleagues during unexpected circumstances soon grew into something more. In July 2005, the HCA Healthcare Hope Fund was formally established as a nonprofit organization dedicated to supporting colleagues and their families during times of need.


Just one month later, Hurricane Katrina devastated communities along the Gulf Coast, including areas where many HCA Healthcare colleagues lived and worked. Once again, colleagues rallied to help one another, and the Hope Fund provided more than $4 million in grants to HCA Healthcare colleagues affected by the storm.


That early response helped establish the spirit of colleagues helping colleagues that continues to guide the Hope Fund more than two decades later. Today, more than 42,000 colleaguescontribute to the Hope Fund each year, helping ensure support is available when colleagues need it.


> **Related story:**[Hurricane Katrina changed how a Nashville healthcare group handles emergencies](https://www.newschannel5.com/news/state/tennessee/davidson-county/how-hurricane-katrina-forever-changed-how-a-nashville-healthcare-giant-handles-natural-disasters)


## **HCA Healthcare colleagues share how the Hope Fund supported them**


During Hope Fund Week, we recognize the generosity that makes this support possible and share the stories of five HCA Healthcare colleagues who turned to the Hope Fund following unexpected circumstances. Their experiences reflect what it means to have support from their HCA Healthcare community behind them.


#### **Hope Fund helps South Carolina nurse focus on recovery after a car accident**


When an unexpected accident left Melanie Tromblee unable to work for nearly six months, the HCA Healthcare Hope Fund helped ease the financial burden so she could focus on healing and getting back to the work she loves.


One evening after leaving work at HCA Healthcare’s[Grand Strand Medical Center](https://www.mygrandstrandhealth.com/) in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, Melanie Tromblee was driving home when a deer struck her car. The accident left her with a back injury that required surgery and temporarily affected the motor function and sensation in her hands and arms.


Melanie, an operating room nurse, has spent more than 26 years building a career around caring for others. She began her healthcare career as a certified nursing assistant before becoming a nurse in 2020. After the accident, she suddenly found herself on the other side of care — facing a long recovery and needing support of her own.


As Melanie worked to regain strength and relearn everyday tasks, she was unable to return to work for nearly six months.


Although Melanie knew about the HCA Healthcare Hope Fund, she hesitated to apply because she worried another colleague might need the assistance more. She completed the application and deleted it five times before ultimately submitting it.


When Melanie learned she had been approved for a Hope Fund grant, the assistance helped with essential household expenses while she focused on her recovery.


> “The Hope Fund took that feeling of drowning away. It made me feel like I could actually breathe again.”


Today, Melanie is back in the operating room and contributes to the Hope Fund herself. She hopes her experience encourages colleagues facing qualifying unexpected circumstances to consider seeking support and reminds them what colleagues can make possible for one another.


#### **Hope Fund supports North Carolina colleague during heart surgery recovery**


Mission Hospital guest services colleague Bill Boeheim spends his days helping patients and families. When he needed support during his own health journey, the HCA Healthcare Hope Fund was there to help him focus on what mattered most — his recovery.


Bill Boeheim is accustomed to helping others through difficult moments. In his guest services role at HCA Healthcare’s[Mission Hospital](https://www.missionhealth.org/locations/mission-hospital) in Asheville, North Carolina, he is often one of the first people families encounter when they arrive at the hospital’s emergency room. He helps loved ones find family members, answers questions and offers reassurance during what can be a difficult time.


After years of being there for others, Bill experienced what it meant to have others there for him when he needed a third open-heart surgery.


Bill had undergone two previous open-heart surgeries and remembered the challenges that came with recovering from his second procedure. As he prepared for another surgery, he knew he would need significant time away from work to recover. At the same time, Bill was helping care for his 85-year-old mother while he and his wife managed household and medical expenses.


When a human resources colleague checked in with Bill and learned what he was navigating, she encouraged him to apply for assistance from the HCA Healthcare Hope Fund. Bill had heard of the Hope Fund but did not realize the type of assistance it could provide. After applying, he received support that helped with essential expenses during the approximately two and a half months he was away from work, giving him one less thing to worry about as he focused on his recovery.


#### **Las Vegas nurse finds hope during daughter’s extended NICU stay**


When Jennie Willis’s daughter, Zoe, arrived at just 26 weeks and spent more than four months in the NICU, the HCA Healthcare Hope Fund helped support Jennie and her family as they naviagted Zoe’s care and recovery.


For HCA Healthcare colleague Jennie Willis and her family, the arrival of their third child unfolded very differently than they hoped. At 24 weeks pregnant, Jennie learned her baby was not receiving enough blood and nutrients through the placenta.


Jennie, a registered nurse in the post-anesthesia care unit at[Sunrise Hospital & Medical Center](https://www.sunrisehealthinfo.com/locations/sunrise-hospital) in Las Vegas, was admitted to nearby HCA Healthcare sister facility[MountainView Hospital](https://www.sunrisehealthinfo.com/locations/mountainview-hospital) . There, her care team worked to safely extend her pregnancy and give her baby more time to grow.


At 26 weeks and three days, Jennie delivered her daughter, Zoe, by C-section. Weighing just 1 pound, 7 ounces, Zoe spent more than four months receiving specialized care in MountainView Hospital’s Level III neonatal intensive care unit (NICU).


Throughout Zoe’s stay, Jennie and her husband balanced time at the hospital with caring for their two older children. Jennie eventually returned to work at Sunrise Hospital & Medical Center while Zoe remained at MountainView Hospital, visiting her daughter during breaks and after her shifts.


As Jennie moved between caring for patients at one HCA Healthcare hospital and being with her daughter at another, support extended beyond Zoe’s clinical care. A MountainView Hospital nurse encouraged Jennie to apply for assistance from the HCA Healthcare Hope Fund. The grant helped with expenses during Zoe’s extended hospitalization, giving the family additional support as they focused on her care and recovery.


Today, Zoe is home and thriving. Jennie hopes her experience encourages other colleagues to recognize that accepting support can be another expression of the community HCA Healthcare colleagues create for one another. Her message to colleagues is to consider applying when they need assistance — and, when they are able, to help extend that same support to someone else.


#### **Texas nurse educator turns to Hope Fund after home damage**


When a storm displaced Cindy Williams from her home, the HCA Healthcare Hope Fund helped her get back on her feet — and back home.


An unexpected storm left HCA Healthcare nursing colleague Cindy Williams temporarily displaced from her Austin, Texas, home. A microburst caused water to enter her condo, damaging the flooring and drywall and forcing Cindy to stay with a friend for several weeks while repairs were completed.


Cindy, a nurse educator at affiliate[St. David’s Medical Center](https://www.stdavids.com/locations/st-davids-medical-center) in Austin, Texas, has spent her HCA Healthcare career helping patients understand what comes next — from preparing for discharge to managing their care once they return home. She was also familiar with the HCA Healthcare Hope Fund from stories she had seen in colleague communications. But when she found herself facing an unexpected event of her own, she initially hesitated to apply.


Knowing other colleagues were also navigating difficult circumstances, Cindy questioned whether she should seek assistance. Her coworkers encouraged her to apply, reminding her that the Hope Fund was there to support eligible colleagues when they need it.


When Cindy learned she would receive a Hope Fund grant, the assistance helped ease the transition back into her home after weeks away. The experience also gave her a new perspective on accepting help. Now, Cindy encourages other colleagues not to hesitate to learn about the resources available to them following an unexpected event. Her message is simple: It is OK to accept support when you need it — because that is exactly why the Hope Fund is there.


#### **Hope Fund support comes full circle for Florida ER nurse**


Nearly a decade after colleagues rallied around Jamie Zemball during a family crisis, she experienced that spirit of support again through the HCA Healthcare Hope Fund.


Jamie Zemball, a nurse with 23 years of experience, joined HCA Healthcare in 2016. Just a few months into her new role at[HCA Florida Lake Monroe Hospital](https://www.hcafloridahealthcare.com/locations/lake-monroe-hospital) her daughter became seriously ill and required life support.


Though Jamie was new to the team, her colleagues quickly rallied around her, donating paid time off so she could spend more time with her daughter. “I can’t really put that into words,” Jamie said, reflecting on the support she received from colleagues who were still getting to know her.


Nearly a decade later, Jamie found herself facing another unexpected health crisis — this time, her own. After experiencing chest pain and becoming increasingly ill, she was diagnosed with pericarditis and blood clots in her lungs. Her recovery kept her away from work for six months.


As Jamie focused on getting better, the extended recovery brought additional challenges for her family of six. This time, support came through the HCA Healthcare Hope Fund.


A Hope Fund grant helped Jamie and her family with essential expenses during her recovery, but she says the impact went beyond financial assistance. “It wound up being enough to just give me a little bit of light at the end of the tunnel,” Jamie said.


For Jamie, the experience reinforced what she first learned as a new HCA Healthcare colleague: support from others can make a meaningful difference during an unexpected time of need. Today, she hopes colleagues recognize how their contributions to the Hope Fund become part of that support for others.


“In the end, it all goes into supporting someone in need,” Jamie said. “Every little bit matters.”
